newsitem.title: USA: US high-yield issues dichotomized, telecoms opt out.
newsitem.headline: US high-yield issues dichotomized, telecoms opt out.

text.p: The high-yield sector appeared split between bloated zero couponed telecommunications issues and names with proven cash flow, dealers on Friday said.

Current market conditions on Friday prompted Teleport Communications Group to postpone its equity and debt offering that were planned to finance 1998 capital requirements, the company said. The debt portion was to total $350 million.
The postponement was the second in as many days. On Thursday, Adelphia Communications Corp's Hyperion Telecommunications postponed its $125 million high-yield offering due to market conditions.

Syndicate officials contend softness in the telecom sector is temporary given the plethora of issues in the past several weeks, however. Still strong demand is demonstrated in industrials and other areas with proven earnings, they said.
In addition, players said the dwindling risk-reward ratio has lessened demand for the lower B-rated issues.

On Friday, Olympic Financial Ltd issued $300 million in 11-1/2 percent 10-year senior notes at par via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities. The notes, rated B2/B-minus, were priced with warrants for five percent of the company.
Market sources were also speculating that WinStar Communications Inc may have to alter a $450 million three-part junk bond offering that is expected to price next week due to market conditions.
WinStar is a competitive local exchange carrier specializing in wireless services.
The 144a deal currently consists of $100 million in senior discount notes, $150 million in senior subordinated discount notes and $200 million in senior secured notes, market sources said.
One analyst suggested the company may have to reduce the amount of the zero coupon segment of the offering in light of slack investor demand for these securities.
A WinStar spokeswoman declined to comment on the offering.
